concepts.title: The Inner Silence of the Sacrificer, Not the Outer Fire
concepts.excerpt: You've seen a fire ritual, or a version of one. Something goes into the flames — ghee, grain, a folded leaf — and someone says svāhā, and the fire takes it.

concepts.title: Dadhīci and the Yoginī-Stambha Mudrā
concepts.excerpt: Indra needs a weapon. The asuras are winning, and the only thing that will work is a vajra made from the bones of a sage who is still using them.

concepts.title: Five Faces, Five Elements, Five Functions
concepts.excerpt: Watch the first video. The teacher counts the faces of Śiva: first this one, second that one, Aghora is third, Tatpuruṣa fourth, Īśāna fifth and on top.

concepts.title: Pītāmbara Vidyā: The Joint Current
concepts.excerpt: Madanāsura goes and gets a boon, and the boon is well chosen: nobody can silence him.

concepts.title: Pañcavaktra Bhairava: The Five Faces
concepts.excerpt: Go stand in front of one. Stone figure, and where the head should be there are five — four at the compass points, a fifth on top, tilted up.

concepts.title: Kabandha Bhairava: The Headless Form
concepts.excerpt: Picture the standard fierce god and you already know the face. Bulging eyes, bared teeth, a tongue out, a garland of skulls.

concepts.title: Kabandha: Bound to the Void
concepts.excerpt: Most spiritual names promise a release. Mokṣa is letting go. Nirvāṇa is a flame going out.

concepts.title: Kabandha and Vīrabhadra: One Hair, Two Accounts
concepts.excerpt: A god's wife has just burned herself alive at her father's sacrifice. He reaches up into his matted hair.

concepts.title: Dhūmavanta Bhairava: The Smoke-Bodied
concepts.excerpt: Sit in front of a fire long enough and you notice there are three things there, not one.

concepts.title: Dhūmāvatī Is Not a Widow
concepts.excerpt: She's old. She's riding a crow. She's wrapped in smoke, and her eyes look like storm clouds coming in.

concepts.title: Dhūmavanta as the Grown Vaṭuka
concepts.excerpt: You know the young one. Vaṭuka Bhairava is the boy-form — wild, wrathful, quick, the version people put at doorways and think of as somehow junior.

concepts.title: Ekavaktra Bhairava: The One-Faced
concepts.excerpt: Brahmā has four. Śiva has five. Skanda has six, and if you keep going through the pantheon the pattern holds: the more a deity has to cover, the more faces he gets.

concepts.title: Yagneśvara: The Vedic Name of Ekavaktra
concepts.excerpt: A ṛṣi has spent a year in penance and something has finally appeared. He asks the obvious question: in which form am I seeing you?

concepts.title: The Ten Sub-Svarūpas of Dhūmavanta
concepts.excerpt: Think about what it takes to guard something that isn't in a building.

concepts.title: Śābara Vidyā and Its Guardian
concepts.excerpt: Most mantras you can write on a card. The syllables are fixed, the order is fixed, and if you say them in that order you have said the mantra.

concepts.title: Khaṇḍobā / Mālāri: The Bhairava Who Hunted
concepts.excerpt: A demon called Malla is losing. He is being beaten by the gods, and he does what everything in this cosmology does when it is beaten — he goes down, escaping to the underworld.

concepts.title: Pātāla Bhairava: The Hundred and Fourth
concepts.excerpt: Most deities come with equipment. A mantra you can be given, a yantra you can draw, a stotra somebody has printed, an image with agreed iconography.

concepts.title: Pātāla Bhairava as Karmic Excavator
concepts.excerpt: Almost every deity in the devotional economy grants something. That is the transaction: you approach, you offer, you ask, and something is given.

concepts.title: The Seven Pātāla Lokas as Consciousness Bands
concepts.excerpt: Here is an observation the source makes in passing and never returns to, and it is the best thing in the episode.

concepts.title: You Do Not Go to Pātāla, You Fall Into It
concepts.excerpt: The episode's own framing, from the material that fronts it: you don't go to Pātāla.

concepts.title: Fourteen Lokas Under One Guardianship
concepts.excerpt: Most cosmological maps give you a stack of worlds and one relation to all of them: you are down here, the good stuff is up there, and the practice is elevation.

concepts.title: The Underground Sanctum: An Architecture That Repeats
concepts.excerpt: Go to a Bhairava temple and you will find the thing you came for. A shrine, an image, a priest, an offering, a queue.

concepts.title: Twelve Jyotirliṅgas, Twelve Bhairavas
concepts.excerpt: The twelve Jyotirliṅgas are the most completed pilgrimage circuit in Śaiva India.

concepts.title: King Parvata and the Settling of the Mountains
concepts.excerpt: There are old stories, the teacher says, in the Śiva Purāṇa and the Devī material, that mountains used to walk.

concepts.title: Bhairava as Liṅga: When Movement Became Stillness
concepts.excerpt: Go back far enough and there is no time, no direction, nothing to count with.

concepts.title: Kālāgni to Jñānāgni
concepts.excerpt: Anyone who has kept a practice for a few years knows this and does not usually have a word for it.

concepts.title: Stambhatva, Kāla-Stambha, Chaitanya-Sthāna
concepts.excerpt: There is a stone in a temple. It doesn't move, it isn't shaped like anything, and people have been walking around it for centuries.

concepts.title: Liṅga-Dhyāna in the Nātha Transmission
concepts.excerpt: Sit in front of a liṅga sometime and notice what actually happens.

concepts.title: Vāmadeva and the Yellow Ash on the Tongue
concepts.excerpt: Vāmadeva works in the cremation grounds at Kāśī. That is his practice — a śmaśāna sādhaka, sitting where the bodies burn.

concepts.title: Alakh Niranjan: The Name at the Doorstep
concepts.excerpt: A man goes from door to door with a bowl. He is a mendicant; this is how he eats.
